newsitem.title: USA: CME hogs and pork bellies see profit taking late.
newsitem.headline: CME hogs and pork bellies see profit taking late.

text.p: Profit taking pared best levels late but both CME hog and pork belly futures finished with gains following the firmer undertone to cash markets, traders said.
Live hogs closed 0.875 higher to unchanged with April up 0.525 at 72.950 cents. Pork bellies finished 1.475 cent higher to unchanged with May up 1.475 at 81.275 cents.

Locals and commission house profit taking developed late but talk of bottoming action in cash pork products, calls for higher cash hog markets Thursday and the continuing Taiwan pork export ban kept hog futures supported, they said.

Cash pork product markets are showing increased interest and this should prompt packers to raise their bids for cash hogs. Another storm moving in from the west may also hamper hog movement Thursday. A bullish chart picture added to the firmer cash outlook to take prices up sharply before the late profit taking developed, they said.

Summer months continued to be supported by an expected rise in U.S. pork exports following an outbreak of foot and mouth disease in Taiwan's hog herd. Adding to the bullish sentiment was talk of a large cull of hogs at Dutch farms to combat a swine fever epidemic there, they added.
"It's just another piece of news that's going to contribute to the strength of the deferred (hog) contracts," said Chuck Levitt, senior livestock analyst for Alaron Trading Corp.

Rand Financials, Refco, Lind-Waldock and Hammer Trading were notable buyers on the advance. In hog options, Refco sold October 72 calls early. A local was a large buyer of June 76/75 put spread on a one-for-two basis. Cargill Investor Services bought October 74 puts, pit sources said.
Pork bellies rose after Tuesday's out-of-town report and reports of a stronger cash belly market, traders said.
"The out-of-town figure was a friendly number plus the strength in the fresh market" gave belly futures a boost, Levitt said.

Users showed increased interest for product after the recent small setback in values. Traders cited reports of cash bellies trading as high as $76 per cwt after being down to $71 earlier in the week, traders said.
CME reported a net in-movement of 255,000 lbs in the weekly out-of-town storage report. This compared with early analysts' estimates of in 250,000 to 500,000 lbs.
Cargill Investor Services, LFG and Rand Financials were early buyers. LFG and Rand sold late, pit sources said.
